# railway_volume (Resource)

A Railway volume, as `railway.Volume`. Mount it with a service's `volume_mounts`. Destroying it deletes the volume and its data.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "environment_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "railway_volume" "postgres" {
  environment_id      = var.environment_id
  name                = "postgres-volume"
  region              = "us-west2"
  size_mb             = 50000
  allow_online_resize = true
  usage_alerts        = [80, 95, 100]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) ID of the Railway environment that holds this volume. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `name` (String) Name of the volume. Railway IaC addresses resources by name, so renaming replaces it.

### Optional

- `allow_online_resize` (Boolean) Resize without stopping the service.
- `fork_from_base_environment` (Boolean) Create the volume in a forked environment from the base environment's data.
- `region` (String) Region the volume lives in.
- `size_mb` (Number) Size in megabytes.
- `usage_alerts` (List of Number) Usage percentages that send an alert, such as `[80, 95, 100]`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<environment_id>/<address>`, for example `c2b9…/volume.web`.
- `live_changes` (List of String) Changes Railway needs to match this configuration, as `railway config plan` lists them. Empty after an apply; a refresh fills it when the live environment drifts, and the next plan applies them.
- `project_id` (String) ID of the Railway project the environment belongs to.
- `railway_id` (String) Railway's ID for this volume.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <environment_id>/volume.<name>
terraform import railway_volume.postgres 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/volume.postgres-volume
```
